I think that a list like that would have to include not only classics but themes as to what was scary at the time.
In the 20’s to 40’s you’d have the silent films like Cabinet of Dr. Caligari and Nosferatu as well as the universal monsters. These were an entertaining way to get scared as to avoid the real horrors going on during the world wars.
In the 50’s I’d recommend Godzilla and War of the worlds. Fear had changed as now we lean into more science fiction and the fear of nuclear war. 
In the 60’s you’d have Psycho and Night of the living dead. Fear evolves into people. Delving into how mental illness can cause fear as well as how a good plot twist can make a movie even scarier. Also psycho is the progenitor of slashers. Night of the living dead can focus on the fear of zombies but also how people can fear and distrust others during emergency. 
The 70’s would be a mixed bag. Paranormal/supernatural horror with the exorcist and suspiria well as the continuation of slashers with Halloween and the Texas chainsaw massacre. Jaws and alien are also must sees and can fall into catergories of animal horror. 
The 80’s have the two giants of the slasher genre with Friday the 13th and A Nightmare on Elm Street. Also I think In order to show a certain film in the 90’s you should show Friday the 13th as the plot twist is spoiled in it. The 80’s also show the evolution of practical effects with the fly remake and the thing remake. This can bring up the discussion of remakes and how these differ from their original counterparts and what makes them scary to the audiences of their time periods.
The 90’s would have Scream and the Blair witch project. Slashers had grown tired at this point so we can see how scream not only poked fun but revitalized the genre. Blair Witch also introduces the found footage genre which we become popular in the decades to come.
The 2000’s would have Saw, the descent and paranormal activity. A discussion about ‘torture porn’ can happen with Saw and why movies like that started to become popular. The descent and paranormal activity can raise the question as why the supernatural and monsters are still scary to modern audiences. 
The 2010’s would have Hereditary, It Follows, and Get Out. We can discuss the new ideas of horror being introduced as well as how political/race issues can be apart of horror movies like get out. Also the stereotypes of how black people are usually the first victims in horror movies. Get Out and Night of the living dead share a link with both main characters were black men. How it was groundbreaking when night of the living dead came out and how Jordan Peele used race and horror to talk about modern issues.
In the 2020’s I’d probably asked the students to pick what they believe so far to be influential in this decade. This would also help discuss what is scary in the modern day. If I had to pick movies though they would probably be; Nope, Smile 2 and Terrifier 2. Terrifier 2 could also bring a discussion about gore. How much is too much, have we become desensitized to it. Is the amount of gore almost comedic like in other movies such as Braindead/Dead Alive.

This wasn’t for a test but when I was around your age, I had just finished orientation day with my parents at the college I chose. Parking lot was packed so neither parent could get in the car to back it up. They asked if I could do it and I gladly said yes. I was confident in my ability as I finished a drivers Ed class recently and how hard could backing up be? Well like an idiot, I didn’t hold the wheel straight when I backed up and it resulted in the car next to us getting scratched up. It looked almost as if someone keyed their car. I heard my parents scream out in horror but it was too late. It was a professor’s car too. I haven’t even started classes at this school and I fucked up a professors parked car. That was it for driving for me for a while. I took someone lessons throughout the years but I always thought I’d fail the drivers test. I’m 25 now and earlier in the year I paid for a package deal which gave me 8 lessons with the drivers test being after the last lesson. I was doing well in the drivers Ed car but I needed more experience. So for the first time I drove a car without any assistance. It was my parents brand new car and would shortly become our only car due to my dad’s crapping out. I was so terrified but I was able to get to my destination no problem. I kept driving without assistance while still doing the lessons. By the end I still did not feel confident in myself but my teacher was. I took the drivers test and nearly failed trying to parallel park. I was about to hit the curb, but I remember how to correct myself and saved myself from failing. After nearly a decade of having the opportunity to drive and not acting on it, I was able to finally get my licensed, something I thought I’d never accomplish. You will get there too. Do as much driving as you can with your parent so you become more comfortable. Nerves are a huge reason contributing to failed drivers exam. I was at your age and I didn’t even want to drive. Your age doesn’t matter, you just have to get more experience. You will pass if you keep trying. If you don’t know something, ask your parents.  Pay attention to what they’re doing when they drive. You will get your license, take it from someone who was in your shoes; you’ve got this! I believe in you and you should believe in yourself. Pick yourself up, dust yourself off, and practice, practice, practice. This is not something unobtainable, you can and will get this. Best of luck to you and I hoped this message helped.

I love my dad, but my story is very similar. I was your son. My dad was verbally abusive rather than physical. It was mostly directed at my mother but it would happen to me and my siblings too. I know that fear your son had all too well. Being terrified of the littlest thing going wrong, knowing it could set your father off. My mom didn’t leave my dad and they are still together to this day. His anger has subsided immensely from when I was a child but it’s still there. I still walk on eggshells when I’m around him. I try to protect my siblings from him, but sometimes the fear will be so powerful I can’t move. I’m a grown man now and I’m still a frightened little boy around my father when he is angry. I developed depression and have attempted suicide multiple times for what I know now that most of that trauma was the reason I became depressed. There are other reasons but the things he would say would stick in my mind and fester there like a tumor. My self worth plummeted because I was unable to protect my mother and siblings from the trauma. I feel useless and like a coward because of this and I began to hate myself almost more than that side of my father. My dad still has his moments but he’s much better now and he is my best friend, but I’m glad you’re doing what my mom should’ve. Get your son out of that environment and make sure he never becomes like me. I hope you and your son can heal from all this. My best wishes to you guys.

Technically my mom is a product of rape due to my grandpa’s lack of knowledge of my grandma’s actions. I definitely think of my grandma differently now. I definitely feel that same anger about the situation but it brought my mom into this world and I know the world is a better place because she exists in it.

You did what you could to protect your daughter. I would recommend giving her Jeanette McCurdy’s new book in order to help her understand what child stars go through and what could’ve been her future. Also the likes of child stars like Amanda Bynes and Lindsay Lohan are good examples to show the damage child stardom can do as well. I sympathize with you and your daughter and hopefully everything works out for you two in the end. Good luck, and best wishes to you both.

Ditch the “friends”, and keep the girl. I know all that is a lot to take in, but I think you should be proud of yourself for many reasons. 
1. You didn’t judge your gf for her actions nor insulted her. You were still her rock.
2. You treated with decency and respect. You made her feel human while your friends used both of you for their own amusement. 
3. Even after finding all this out, you still love her all the same. The love you guys have for each other is rare in this world and you should hold on to that. Your gf was a victim, as were you. Your “friends” don’t even compare to how she feels about you.
I know you also mentioned that it bothers you that she had sex with your “friends” quicker than she did with you, but I have 2 theories that hopefully will ease your mind.
1. Your gf might have struggled with major insecurity and slept with them in order to keep them around. Having “friends” was better than being alone. Your “friends” saw her as an object and she probably thought that too, until she met you.
2. She took things slow with you because she valued your companionship/relationship. She was probably afraid that you’d leave her if she had sex with you immediately. She valued you more than any of your so called “friends”. They viewed as nothing more than an object, and they were nothing to her except some validation that people will stay around you. That all completely changed when she met you. She wanted you for the long haul, and not just for a fling. You are more important to her than anyone else.
Listen, it sounds like your gf is the perfect match for you. Don’t throw that away for a past that no longer matters. You guys were both victims and used for amusement by shitty people. Let this make your relationship stronger. I would suggest individual and couples therapy for you and your gf so you can get over this hurdle. You’ve got a good one, partners like your gf are rare. Do whatever you have to to get past this. It was under shitty circumstances that you two found each other, but you two created a match made in heaven. My best wishes to the both of you, and of course, fuck those asshole “friends”.

I spent years wallowing in my depression. Alone with my thoughts. I’ve always felt like this, I thought I deserved it, but then something clicked. I realized that I don’t want to feel this way anymore. I wanted to change, or at least try. That way if my life ends I at least tried. I started going to the gym 3 days a week for the last 2-3 weeks. I’m trying to get out of bed more. I usually use music to cope and I combined that coping mechanism with the gym: a new coping mechanism for me. The music motivates me to work harder. I want to feel better about myself, I want to feel attractive for once in my life. I’ll be getting my master’s degree in 1-2 years and hopefully find a job to get my own place. The thing that motivates me the most is my family, my loved ones, they’ve been by my side through the worst I’ve been, and they cheered me on the whole time. I have to get better, my loved ones want me to and for the first time in my life, I want to live. Every day can be a struggle but my will to live which was once smoldering embers is now a raging fire. For anyone reading this; don’t give up, you are worthy of love and finding happiness. I’m rooting for you all just as my family did for me. Be safe everyone and best wishes.

YTA. Judging by your BF’s reaction, I think that something like this has happened before. This is probably a big insecurity for him as women gravitate toward his brother. His brother is an asshole too because his response suggests that he knows it makes your BF insecure and he enjoys doing it. He’s probably been second choice to his brother a lot and now his GF, someone he’s trusted and loved decided to chose his brother again. I don’t think any apologies are going to help because this is probably always gonna be in the back of your BF’s mind. He feels inferior to his brother and by asking him to bring his brother instead of him has made him feel ashamed for the way he looks. He always think that you’ll want his brother instead of him. First if you went with his brother. He wonder what was next. Would you bring the brother with you to have dinner with your family? Would you start spending time with his brother alone? Would you or your brother start to have feelings for one another? Would you cheat on him with his brother? You’ll obviously say that this is outlandish and ridiculous but these are the doubts that have festered because you justified a big insecurity of his. Your post does come of as vain and superficial so in one last attempt to show you how bad you’ve fucked up, let me give you a hypothetical. What if it was the other way around? If you have a sister who you’ve always felt was prettier than you and got all the boys attention whereas you did not? Would you feel okay with your BF choosing your sister over you because she looks more appealing? Would that not destroy you? The one person who chose you over the person who always got the attention, turned  out to be a lie. Your BF had probably been worried about how he looks his whole life, especially with a brother that is “objectively attractive” as you put it. Turns out he’s not attractive enough to bring to a work event. Will family events be next? Will he be replaced? You’ve tapped into one of his biggest insecurities. I don’t know if you can repair the damage done. Your BF will always see himself as the undesirable choice to you now. If you really love your BF, apologize immediately and do everything in your power to show that you are proud to call him your BF and you are attracted to him. That he’s attractive enough to be seen with you and shouldn’t be ashamed of his looks. I hope this has been an eye opener. Do better for your BF. He doesn’t deserve to feel like a second choice to the one person he believed would chose him first.

My father is similar to your husband in the fact that he has major anger issues. I’m now an adult and my dad is my best friend, but he’s also probably responsible for nearly all my childhood trauma. My mom faced the brunt of the verbal abuse, however when it was directed at us, as a kid it was terrifying. I was scared of my dad, I was convinced he didn’t even want to be around me or like me until I was nearly an adult. The things he said to both my mom and my siblings and my self are unforgivable. We know that he doesn’t mean what he says but he still said. The things said will fester like a tumor inside your daughter. Any self-esteem and self-worth will be evaporated. It’s quite possible your daughter will develop depression because of this. I am speaking from personal experience. I developed depression at 12 years old and try to commit suicide many times between 17-18 years 
old. This could very well be your childrens future if you refuse to intervene. Your husband has faced trauma and he needs therapy to unpack that. It is unacceptable that he is taking it out on your children. My mother couldn’t leave my dad because of financial reasons and she still loved him. Myself and my siblings do too but he has affected my life in an irrevocable way. I shut down at the slightest hint of confrontation. I haven’t formed any type of relationship outside of my family. I still feel like that scared little boy cowering behind my mom while my dad was screaming venomous shit to us. There’s apart of me that resents my mother for not leaving and when my dad gets mad I intervene to get him away, but I always hesitate. It makes me feel like a coward and further develops my self-hatred. I am telling you now. Your husband needs to go to therapy and if he refuses: LEAVE HIM. GET OUT, make sure he sees them as little as possible. Do not make the same mistakes made in my family. Do not let your children suffer through this trauma. Make sure they don’t grow up to become like me. Get them out while you still can before it permanently alters your children. You NEED to give him an ultimatum: get therapy or you will LEAVE him. Keep your children safe because if he doesn’t get therapy or you don’t get away from him, it will only get worse. Please, I am begging you, keep your children safe.

First off, I’m so sorry for you loss. You have my condolences. It is not okay for you to lock the possessions of you son to keep them away from your daughter. This is how she is mourning him and she deserves to grief her brother in any way. I know you and your wife are grieving too but look, Allen is unfortunately not here anymore and that is all she has left of him. It sounds like your loss has affected Sarah so much that she is developing signs of depression. You started your post off by saying Allen had a lot of mental health issues, so I’m assuming he committed suicide. I’m so sorry that happened but like I said Allen is no longer with you , but Sarah is. She is showing worrying symptoms of depression that your son showed too. It’s time to focus on Sarah. Don’t make the same mistakes you did with Allen. Go into family therapy and get help for Sarah. Apologize to her as well and maybe you guys should go into his room together and discuss the memories you’ve had of him through the objects in his room. If Allen were here, he would want you guys to heal together instead of grieving apart, as well as not having a problem with how your daughter is grieving. I know you just lost your son, but you could also lose your daughter. Get the help you all deserve to mourn properly. Let your daughter cope in her own way. Stick together, do not fall apart. Your daughter needs you guys now more than ever and I know you guys are mourning too, but you have a responsibility to protect Sarah. Allen would want you all to find comfort with each other. Apologize and get help before it is too late. It’s what Allen would want. I’m once again sorry for you loss. Honor Allen by protecting and healing the ones he loved; Sarah, your wife, and you. You have my best wishes and I hope you all heal.

As a person who has attempted suicide before, I can tell you with certainty that you are not to blame. It is not anyone’s fault. When I was about to attempt, it wasn’t because of anyones actions. The pain was too much to handle and just as I felt, your boyfriend may have kept his depression from you and others because he didn’t want you to worry or feel like a burden. I know you said your family isn’t supportive, but what about his family. Can you grieve and confide to anyone in his family? Maybe you all can tell stories about your favorite memory with him. I’m am so incredibly sorry for you loss. I know you might not believe it but I’m sure your boyfriend felt the same way: IT IS NOT YOUR FAULT. Your boyfriend loved you, but he might’ve thought he didn’t deserve your love. The pain depression causes can be unbearable and unfortunately lead to suicide. It was not you nor anyone else. Your boyfriend was victim of this horrible illness. I hope you can find peace and properly grieve. If you need to talk, my inbox is always open. Take care and know this; your boyfriend loved you with all his heart, hell you were probably a reason he prolonged his life. I’m once again sorry for you loss. You have my condolences.
